summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-09 (window Oct 3–9). Three candidates, all institutional ballot errors, each backed by two opened accepted sources. (1) Colorado: about 800,000 ballots in four counties wrongly include the Front Range Passenger Rail tax question (CPR, CBS Colorado, Gazette). (2) Athens-Clarke County, Ga.: a mailing-list error sends a second absentee ballot to 1,154 voters (WSB-TV, CBS Atlanta). (3) Oxford, Maine: a printer's packaging error sends some voters the wrong ballot style (Press Herald, WGME). Several items set aside earlier only for timing now fall inside the window. Search capacity ran out before I found a non-election alternate. Genius: GENIUS scan for 2026-10-09 (window Oct 3–9). I'm submitting one candidate, and it has a sourcing caveat. A Science paper published Oct. 8 by Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (USGS) scientists analyzes Kilauea's 54 lava fountains. I opened and checked the Science News article (Oct. 8). The second source, Phys.org (Oct. 9), returned 'url_not_accessible' every time I tried to open it. Its URL and text, including the corroboration passage, come only from the search tool's copy of the page. So this candidate does not fully meet the rule that two pages must be opened, and the mechanical check against Phys.org may fail. Ars Technica also covered the study (found through a link on an aggregator), but the fetch tool would not open it. My search quota ran out early in the run, which limited how many alternates I could find and source. Most other in-window items were outside the US, published before the window, or had only one accepted source. No genius story met the standard; nothing published. The verified facepalm story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.reason: quote not found on page (sciencenews.org)

candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.reason: an earlier candidate was published

candidates.reason: an earlier candidate was published

candidates.headline: Nearly 600 Floyd County, Ind., voters get early ballots missing the county commissioner race
candidates.reason: In the date window (Oct. 6–9). I opened only one accepted source (LPM). The WHAS11 page couldn't be reached twice, and WDRB and News and Tribune aren't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Anthropic AI model submits a false homicide tip to the Philadelphia police website
candidates.reason: The story centers on an unsolved homicide, so a killing is involved. That falls under the exclusion even though the error itself hurt no one.

candidates.headline: Kendall County, Ill., sends 300 wrong mail-in ballots to two precincts
candidates.reason: The ballots were mailed Sept. 24, before the window. I found only one accepted source (Shaw Local).

candidates.headline: Champaign County, Ill., suspends early voting after ballot errors
candidates.reason: Coverage is still only on outlets not on the accepted list (WCIA, IPM Newsroom, Fox Illinois, News-Gazette, Capitol News Illinois, Yahoo).

candidates.headline: UnitedHealthcare letters wrongly tell members eight clinicians had died
candidates.reason: The letters are dated Sept. 11, and the Star Tribune first reported it around Oct. 1. Both are before the 7-day window.

candidates.headline: University of Utah Health and Harvard team find phage proteases trigger CBASS bacterial immunity (Science)
candidates.reason: The only source opened was ScienceDaily (Oct. 9). The Science publication date (vol. 394, issue 6819) could not be confirmed as inside the window, and no second accepted source was opened.

candidates.headline: Webb studies 21 extreme debris disks as signs of planet-scale collisions (Space Science Institute, Boulder)
candidates.reason: According to the NASA write-up carried by ScienceDaily, the paper was published in The Astrophysical Journal on Oct. 1, which is before the window.

candidates.headline: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 splashes down off Los Angeles after 237 days in space (Oct. 8)
candidates.reason: A routine crew return rather than a specific new achievement. The only sources opened were ScienceDaily and NASA, and SpaceX was a recent genius subject.

candidates.headline: CHIME telescope detects hydrogen glow from 9 billion years ago on its own
candidates.reason: A Canadian telescope and a University of British Columbia-led team. Not in the US.

candidates.headline: Physicists create and observe 'Bethe strings' predicted in 1931
candidates.reason: Research by the University of Innsbruck in Austria. Not in the US.

candidates.headline: Golden-yellow coral prompts a new octocoral family
candidates.reason: Found on seamounts off Costa Rica. Not in the US.

candidates.headline: Protist found with a genetic code where UAA and UAG code for different amino acids
candidates.reason: Research by the Earlham Institute in the UK. Not in the US.

candidates.headline: Stanford's Sergiu Pașca team grows human cortical organoids filling a mouse cortex (Nature)
candidates.reason: The paper and its coverage date to mid-September 2026. Only the print issue is dated Oct. 8, so it is too old.

candidates.headline: Quadruped robot runs a marathon on a single battery charge (Nature)
candidates.reason: Developed by KAIST in South Korea, and published online in September. Not in the US and too old.

candidates.reason: Still no accepted publisher found. The coverage is KRDO, Fox21 and the academy's own release, and the academy page could not be opened.

candidates.headline: Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize (Oct. 9)
